newsitem.title: GERMANY: Helaba sees fall in 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Helaba sees fall in 1996 profit.

text.p: Publicly-owned German regional bank Landesbank Hessen-Thueringen Girozentrale said on Thursday it expected a fall in operating profit in 1996.
The bank said its operating profit after risk provisions fell by 2.8 percent to 154.6 million marks in the first six months of 1996 compared with six twelfths of the full-1995 result.

The bank, the regional bank for the states of Hesse and east German Thuringia, said 1996 earnings would be hit by heavy investment in computer systems and in the expansion of its business in London and its east German base in Erfurt.
"Against this background, the management board expects an operating profit for 1996 that will lag behind the previous year," Helaba said in a statement.
Risk provisions in the first half fell to 22.2 million marks from 28.4 million while net interest income grew by 17.4 percent to 525.1 million marks, Helaba said.
Net commission income fell 16.2 percent to 51.4 million marks. The bank made a loss of 22.5 million marks from own-account trading after a profit of 48.9 million.
Administration costs, which slipped by 0.6 percent to 393 million marks in the first half, would rise "disproportionately" during the second half, Helaba said.
The balance sheet total expanded by 6.2 percent to 166.9 billion marks while lending rose 4.4 percent to 119.8 billion, the bank said.
